items.note: Both parts of the original claim are answered by the loop-9 rewrite at 598e61a2 (lab.json notes, line 87) and the record's not-covered sentence at 8135e3b5. Part (1), the ambiguous 'ends at the expected values': the text now says a finished animation on the checklist or a tag shows only what it holds after it ends, its last keyframe if it fills forwards and otherwise its unanimated values, and gives as an example a paused, delayed or very long animation that does not hold its effect after it ends. Part (2), the unscoped finish clause: the finish step is now scoped to 'the checklist and the two tags', matching lines 137-144 of tests/layout.test.mjs, and 'every other animation, on any element' is read as it is at that moment. I checked this end to end with the full public suite on fresh copies of the completed work at 598e61a2, one probe rule appended each, 2 runs each. A paused scale hold on both tags with the default fill passed all 12 tests (2 of 2). The same hold with forwards fill failed task 11 only (2 of 2). A finite scale animation on .page with a 10-second delay and forwards fill passed all 12 (2 of 2), although the page later draws the tags smaller. All three outcomes are what the new text predicts. Two precision notes, not findings, because neither changes any pass or fail the text predicts. First, 'it measures at one moment' is one moment per window size, so two in all. A timeline probe through the lab's withPage helper, 3 runs, read document.timeline.currentTime as constant inside each window's evaluate (also after a 50 ms busy wait) and about 44 to 61 ms later in the second window. The same notes already say two window sizes, and a second reading can only catch more. Second, 'its last keyframe' is loose for reversed or fractional-iteration playback, where the held value is the value at the animation's end; the fail-safe outcome is unchanged. The text is general, says 'Examples include', and README line 17 and task 11 Outcome are unchanged.

The original claim was that 'that changes a width or padding' limited every listed kind of animation, so held scale and zoom read as always caught, and that 'paused' was no longer a correct general example. Neither applies to the current bytes. The residual is now stated by timing and by what is measured, not by property. 'Any animation that changes the drawn size at some other moment can therefore go undetected' covers held scale, zoom, width and padding alike. 'Paused' appears only qualified, as an animation 'that does not hold its effect after it ends'; my probes confirm that a default-fill paused scale hold on the tags passes and a forwards-filled one fails task 11. 'Changing a width or padding' now qualifies only the endless example, and the examples are introduced as examples, not a complete set. The 'rejects a non-identity transform' sentence is now followed directly by the measuring-moment statement, so it no longer implies that held scale or zoom is always caught. lab.json and the record's not-covered list agree.

The original claim was that an endless identity-start scale pulse on an element around the checklist (.page, body) passes, often or always, and that no residual statement named it. Under the owner's option A, detection is not asked for, so it is judged on wording. The rewrite deleted the loop-8 phrase 'in some or all runs'. The new general sentence still covers this case: every other animation 'on any element' is read 'as it is at that moment', and 'any animation that changes the drawn size at some other moment can therefore go undetected'. The examples name 'an endless animation' and 'any animation on an element around the checklist'. 'Can go undetected' is honest about the run-to-run variation the original finding observed. The test bytes are unchanged since 80eff5af (git diff --quiet 7e1a2af6 598e61a2 over tests/, README, starter/ and expected/), and README task 11 Outcome forbids the case.

The test file is byte-identical to 80eff5af. I re-read lines 155-167 (unscaledNow) at 598e61a2. While any animation on the element is not finished, only none and 1 count. Identity end values count only when every animation on the element has finished. The pinned inline styles on .site-aside are saved (lines 184-186) and restored after each window (lines 232-237), so the second window's checklist checks are live. The record's matrix lists endless pulses that start at identity on the tags and the checklist as failing variants. The lab.json sentence 'while an animation is still running on the element only none and 1 count' matches the code; that branch also covers paused endless animations, as the code comment says. The full-suite variant probes I ran did not target this case. The solved run at 598e61a2 passed all 12 tests (7 runs, all 12 passing).

This is an owner-accepted residual, judged only on how honestly it is stated. The README is unchanged (sha256 matches the loop-6 to loop-8 bytes). Line 17 says 'It does not catch every animation, so task 11 also asks you to keep the checklist layout static'. Task 11 Outcome (line 141) scopes the static rule to the checklist, the two tags and the elements around them that affect their layout, and allows decorative effects elsewhere. Nothing tells learners that held animations are acceptable. The maintainer-facing statement (lab.json line 87 and the record's not-covered list) now describes exactly the original cases: a paused, very long, or long-delayed backwards-filled hold that does not hold its effect after it ends, which finish() removes before measuring. My default-fill paused probe confirmed that such a case passes all 12 tests, as stated.
